content:
The fusion of artificial intelligence and interactive design has transformed the creative process. With tools like OpenAI’s image generation and Python’s Streamlit framework, it’s now possible to create interactive, AI-powered web apps with minimal code. In this blog, we’ll walk you through the process of building a Streamlit application that generates stunning AI images based on a user prompt and allows users to apply creative filters and download their enhanced artwork.

🔧 What You’ll Build

You’ll create a web app where users can:

  • Enter a prompt to generate AI images
  • Select how many images (1–5) and their size
  • View the generated images in a gallery
  • Apply filters like Grayscale, Sepia, High Contrast, and Brightness Boost
  • Download the filtered images directly

📦 Tools & Technologies

  • Python
  • Streamlit for interactive UI
  • OpenAI API for image generation
  • Pillow (PIL) for image editing
  • Certifi to handle HTTPS requests securely

💡 Core Features and How They Work

1. Prompt-Based Image Generation with OpenAI

The app leverages OpenAI’s image generation endpoint. Users can enter any text-based prompt, like “A futuristic cityscape at dusk”, and get high-quality images in return.

response = client.images.generate(prompt=prompt, n=1, size=size)

Each image is fetched securely using requests and certifi to avoid SSL certificate issues.

2. Interactive Image Gallery

The generated images are displayed in a neat column layout using st.columns, offering a side-by-side view depending on the number selected.

cols = st.columns(num_images)
for i in range(num_images):
    with cols[i]:
        st.image(images[i], caption=f"Generated Image {i + 1}")

3. Artistic Filters with Pillow

You can choose from a set of filters to enhance your images creatively:

  • Grayscale: Converts the image to black and white
  • Sepia: Gives it a warm, vintage tone
  • High Contrast: Doubles the contrast for a more striking look
  • Increase Brightness: Makes the image glow brighter
if filter_choice == "Sepia":
    img_with_filter = ImageOps.colorize(ImageOps.grayscale(img), "#704214", "#C0C0C0")

4. Instant Download of Filtered Images

Each filtered image is converted to a downloadable .png file using a BytesIO buffer and made available with a st.download_button.

st.download_button(label=f"Download Filtered Image {i + 1}", data=img_bytes,
                   file_name=f"filtered_image_{i + 1}_{filter_choice.lower()}.png", mime="image/png")

🎨 Try It Yourself!

Here’s how the final app will behave:

  1. You enter a creative prompt like “An underwater kingdom of glowing jellyfish”
  2. The app generates 3–5 beautiful AI images
  3. You select “Sepia” to give it a nostalgic tone
  4. You instantly download your new filtered artwork!

🛠️ Final Thoughts

This project is perfect for artists, hobbyists, content creators, or anyone interested in AI-generated visuals. By combining the power of OpenAI and Streamlit, you’ve built an interactive tool that not only sparks creativity but also demonstrates the potential of generative AI in user-friendly applications.

Whether you're showcasing your AI art, experimenting with filters, or simply playing with ideas—this app makes creativity more accessible than ever.

🔗 Source Code Snippet

You can customize and extend the functionality by:

  • Adding more filter effects (e.g., blur, edge detection)
  • Saving original vs. filtered comparisons
  • Sharing artworks via social media APIs

🚀 Ready to Launch?

Deploy your Streamlit app to platforms like Streamlit Cloud, Heroku, or Render for easy access and sharing. Just make sure to secure your apikey.py and never expose your OpenAI API key in public repos.

Start generating your AI masterpieces today and turn your prompts into digital art with just a few clicks!

Python Code:

import os
import certifi
import streamlit as st
from openai import OpenAI
from apikey import apikey  # Store your OpenAI key in apikey.py
import requests
from PIL import Image, ImageEnhance, ImageOps
from io import BytesIO

# Set up the OpenAI API key
os.environ['OPENAI_API_KEY'] = apikey
OpenAI.api_key = apikey
client = OpenAI()

# List of available filters
filters = ["None", "Grayscale", "Sepia", "High Contrast", "Increase Brightness"]

# Streamlit UI setup
st.title("AI-Generated Art Gallery with Custom Filters")
st.write("Enter a prompt, generate up to 5 images, and apply custom filters.")

# User input: Prompt and number of images
prompt = st.text_input("Enter the image prompt:", "A futuristic cityscape at dusk")
num_images = st.slider("Number of images to generate:", 1, 5, 3)
size = st.selectbox("Select image size:", ["1024x1024", "512x512", "256x256"])

if st.button("Generate Images"):
    st.write(f"Generating {num_images} images for: '{prompt}'")
    images = []

    for i in range(num_images):
        response = client.images.generate(prompt=prompt, n=1, size=size)
        image_url = response.data[0].url

        # Fetch and store the images
        img_response = requests.get(image_url, verify=certifi.where())
        img = Image.open(BytesIO(img_response.content))
        images.append(img)

    # Display generated images in a gallery format
    st.write("Generated Images:")
    cols = st.columns(num_images)

    for i in range(num_images):
        with cols[i]:
            st.image(images[i], caption=f"Generated Image {i + 1}")

    # Apply filters to images
    st.write("Apply Filters to Your Images:")
    filter_choice = st.selectbox("Choose a filter to apply:", filters)

    for i, img in enumerate(images):
        st.write(f"Image {i + 1}:")
        img_with_filter = img

        if filter_choice == "Grayscale":
            img_with_filter = ImageOps.grayscale(img)
        elif filter_choice == "Sepia":
            img_with_filter = ImageOps.colorize(ImageOps.grayscale(img), "#704214", "#C0C0C0")
        elif filter_choice == "High Contrast":
            enhancer = ImageEnhance.Contrast(img)
            img_with_filter = enhancer.enhance(2.0)
        elif filter_choice == "Increase Brightness":
            enhancer = ImageEnhance.Brightness(img)
            img_with_filter = enhancer.enhance(1.5)

        st.image(img_with_filter, caption=f"Filtered Image {i + 1} ({filter_choice})", use_column_width=True)

        # Provide an option to download the filtered image
        img_bytes = BytesIO()
        img_with_filter.save(img_bytes, format="PNG")
        img_bytes.seek(0)
        st.download_button(label=f"Download Filtered Image {i + 1}", data=img_bytes,
                           file_name=f"filtered_image_{i + 1}_{filter_choice.lower()}.png", mime="image/png")
